result:
I wrote the API to `blog_api.py`, and a curl run against it worked for every operation I tried. That run covered create, partial update, full update, list, delete, a 404 after delete, a 401 with no key, and a 400 for malformed JSON. I didn't test the `limit`/`offset` query parameters, the 405 responses (POST to `/posts/<id>`, or PUT/PATCH/DELETE on `/posts`) or the 413 body-size limit.

**Run it:** `BLOG_API_KEY=yourkey python3 blog_api.py`. If you don't set the key, the server generates one and prints it at startup.

It listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` and stores posts in `blog.db`. Set `BLOG_DB` to use a different file.

**Endpoints** (every request needs an `X-API-Key` header):

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/posts` | List posts, with optional `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) and `?offset=` |
| POST | `/posts` | Create a post from `{"title", "content", "author"?}` |
| GET | `/posts/<id>` | Read one post |
| PUT | `/posts/<id>` | Replace a post (`title` and `content` required) |
| PATCH | `/posts/<id>` | Update only the fields you send |
| DELETE | `/posts/<id>` | Delete a post (returns 204) |

Errors come back as JSON like `{"error": "..."}`, with status codes 400, 401, 404, 405, 413 or 500. Request bodies over 1 MB are rejected.

Creating a post returns 201 but doesn't send a `Location` header.
